subtype: Approach: buffer planning before the viva [Action]
passage: Kishore, you asked what I would tell juniors, so here is my plan, Parul's plan. Our viva was on the 28th. We picked the 14th as our code freeze, and I wrote it on the door of our lab cupboard so nobody could pretend. I said to the team, "Something will slip. It always does. That is why the last two weeks are for testing, writing up, and rehearsing, not for new features." Sure enough, the login bug ate five days. Our friends who had planned to finish on the 27th were coding at midnight before the viva. We were only tired, not panicking. In the rehearsal a senior asked us about our test data, and we had an answer.

qa.q: On which date did the team freeze the code?
qa.a: They froze the code on the 14th.

qa.q: What is Parul feeling as the team runs into the login bug?
qa.a: Parul is tired but steady rather than panicked, because the buffer means a slip can be absorbed.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Parul add if the buffer is still not enough, and why?
qa.a: They could cut the least important feature early, because dropping something planned protects the testing and the rehearsal.

qa.q: How might the friends who planned to finish on the 27th see this plan?
qa.a: They would likely see it as cautious now, but they were the ones coding at midnight, so they might later want the same slack.

grounding: Shows planning to finish coding early and reserving the last two weeks for testing, the report and rehearsal, expecting that something will slip.

subtype: Approach: buffer planning before the viva [Action]
passage: I'm the lab assistant in the computer science block, so I see every final-year team in the last month. Most of them are here at midnight in April. Hemant and Pranav's team was different. In January, Hemant wrote on the lab whiteboard: "Code freeze: 15 March. Deadline: 31 March." Pranav asked why so early. Hemant said, "Because something will go wrong, and I don't know what yet." They froze their code on the 15th. On the 18th, testing found a bug in the payment screen that took four days to fix. On the 24th, the report printer broke and they had to reprint elsewhere. On the 28th, they rehearsed the viva twice in this room. On the 31st, they submitted at eleven in the morning and went for lunch. I can't read minds, but they didn't look like people who'd been up all night.

qa.q: What was the code freeze date?
Why did Hemant want the code freeze so early?
qa.a: Hemant felt sure something would go wrong and was wary of surprises, wanting time left to handle them.

qa.q: What else could the team add to the final fortnight?
qa.a: They could ask someone outside the team to try the app, since fresh eyes often find bugs the builders miss.

qa.q: How does the lab assistant see this team compared with others?
qa.a: The lab assistant notices they finish calmly and go for lunch, while most teams are in the lab at midnight in April.

grounding: Shows a team finishing coding two weeks early and keeping the last fortnight for testing, the report and rehearsal, expecting something to slip.

subtype: Approach: buffer planning before the viva [Action]
passage:
January. Aparna set out the project calendar in the team's shared sheet. "Coding ends on 1 March. The deadline is 15 March. Those two weeks are for testing, printing the report and one full rehearsal." Chetan frowned. "That's two weeks of not coding." "That's two weeks of fixing whatever breaks," Aparna said.
1 March. They stopped adding features, though Chetan had one more idea he loved. Aparna wrote it on a list titled "After the viva".
9 March. Testing had found three bugs; two were fixed in a day, one took four. The report was printed. On the 13th they rehearsed the viva in front of two juniors, who asked about data privacy, a question none of them had prepared for. They worked out an answer together that evening. On the 15th, when the examiner asked the very same privacy question, Chetan answered it smoothly and glanced at Aparna.

qa.q: How did Chetan feel about stopping coding on 1 March?
qa.a: Chetan was reluctant, having one more idea he loved, and frowned at two weeks without coding.

qa.q: What else could the team do with ideas like Chetan's?
qa.a: Keep them on the After the viva list and choose the best for a later version, so ideas aren't lost but don't threaten the deadline.

qa.q: How might the two juniors see the rehearsal?
qa.a: The juniors get a preview of a viva and help the team by asking a question they hadn't prepared for.

grounding: Illustrates a team planning to stop coding two weeks before the deadline, using the buffer for testing, the report and a rehearsal that pays off.
